chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: Rebelling against the priestly image and returning to piano
summary: Torn between his father's saintly expectations and street reality, Thompson drops the violin as too feminine and goes back to piano; his friends are heavy weights.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: now thinking about this, this is actually when I started molding my entertaining personality, and I'm getting away from gradually being a minister because I don't seem to fit in that environment as a minister, and I'm beginning to rebel against this priestly image, you see. The combination of my interest in sports, and participating with physical combat, and all of these things, plus -- and I hate to inject this--but the violent sources of racial conflict.
Yes.

All these things had to do with changing my viewpoints about music, and my listening ear, and my rebellion against this atmosphere that I was growing up in. In other words at 12 years old I realized that I was growing up in a dual atmosphere, one that my father required me to be a saintly gentleman, and immediately when I would go -- on my way to school I'd find out that I was not living in that world of Jesus Christ, but a world of reality where there was physical strife and conflict, you know.
Yes,yes.
So in other words this had to do with my choice of music at that age, that we were talking about. As I said, going up in those hills and casting, the decisions and all that.
Yes.
So in other words my golf career
ended rather suddenly too and I went back to playing the piano this time.
Oh, you went back to piano.

Yes. I realized that the violin was a little too feminine for me. I think that's what you might say would be the explanation of it, you know, as I grew into manhood early. Because all of my friends were always larger boys, and to this day most of my friends are heavy weights. Isn't that funny?
It is funny.
I'm a bantam weight, and all of my best friends have been heavy weights.
Isn't that funny.

Extremely heavy weights, and we have tussled -- I've actually tussled with heavy weights, and we have a thing together that seems to be an understanding. This is something I'd have to go into. I guess it would be some discussion for somebody in the field of psychiatry.
Yes, they would know what's in the back of all that.
Why does a big man take to me, why does a little man meet such a big man.
Yes, that's funny right.
But all my friends are heavy weights, but I think it's this physical contact that I've had, perhaps

in my early life, as an athlete, that has brought this about. I used to play football until I got the wind knocked out of me and I realized that this wasn't for me. My father was watching me too, incidentally. He tried to help me do anything I wanted to do.
That's wonderful.

Right up until the time I left home. And he didn't approve of that, but I'll tell you about that later when we get into that at a later time of my life when I finally left home, left school. But I want to try to cover everything I can.
